A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PBHC research and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F. The later version's additions and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulation comparisons, motion-processing experiments, ablations, and real-world G1 results, including ten Tai Chi trials.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds PBHC oracle results and training curves for three motions.

M1.justification: Section 5.3 introduces an auxiliary PBHC oracle variant that overlooks partial-observability and action-smoothness constraints. This is a limited training adaptation; the main motion-processing pipeline, adaptive tracking update, and deployable actor-critic design remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The video/AMASS/LAFAN motion collection, filtering examples, and simulation and real-world G1 tasks are retained. The oracle evaluation and learning curves use existing motion coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Ours (Oracle) as an evaluated comparison variant in all three difficulty tiers. OmniH2O, ExBody2, and MaskedMimic remain, as do the existing ablation comparators.

E3.justification: V2 adds an oracle comparison with relaxed observability and action-smoothness constraints, plus training diagnostics measuring episode length and reward over training steps. Existing tracking metrics, 1,000-rollout evaluations, and documented training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 5.6 and Figure 9 examine training stability through episode-length and reward trajectories for Jabs Punch, Tai Chi, and Roundhouse Kick. Existing tracking-factor ablations, contact-mask analyses, and motion-correction demonstrations are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly reports two-sided permutation tests through significance markers at p < 0.05. Three-seed training and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged; no increase in repeated runs is stated.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds oracle PBHC scores, including global body-position errors of 45.02, 66.85, and 79.25 mm across the difficulty tiers, and significance outcomes. Figure 9 adds training trajectories. These oracle scores use relaxed conditions; all previously reported numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The optimization equations, assumptions, and Appendix A derivation are unchanged. New bullets in Section 3.2.2 explain the existing inner and outer objectives without adding mathematical reasoning or formal results.

C1.justification: The central claims about physics-based motion processing, adaptive tracking, superior tracking accuracy, and real-world highly dynamic skills retain their meaning. The abstract and conclusion preserve the same contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.6 newly interprets the learning curves as evidence of stability, convergence around 20k steps, and efficiency. Section 5.3 reframes comparison with MaskedMimic through the oracle experiment. The stated deployment limitations and broader-impact discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The added checklist explicitly affirms open code/data access and points to supplemental material. This is an additional availability statement, whose fulfillment cannot be verified from the PDFs. The project link and detailed implementation information in Appendices B–D are unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction replaces discussion of ASAP's four stages and MoCap requirement with a distinction emphasizing PBHC's simulation-based feasibility and agility improvements. Both versions cite the same 58 works; publication-metadata updates do not add research coverage.

P1.justification: V2 adds explanatory optimization bullets, a learning-curves subsection, and a NeurIPS checklist, alongside localized wording, funding, and bibliographic edits. The main narrative and technical appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains oracle rows, significance markers, and an expanded caption; Figure 9 adds two learning-curve panels. Existing figures and Table 2 are repositioned, and appendix figures are renumbered without substantive visual changes.

improvement.justification: The oracle comparison addresses v1's acknowledged mismatch with MaskedMimic, while the optimization explanation and training curves improve clarity and assessment. The gain is limited: oracle and permutation-test details remain sparse, and Figure 9's continuing Tai Chi reward increase weakens v2's broad convergence-around-20k interpretation.
